reasoning: Single macro body (walnut-kernel) with one meso sub-region (walnut-rim), scoring componentCount 1.
Silhouette scores 2 (not 1): unlike chestnut/olive's near-radial forms, the bilateral two-lobe/groove fold is NOT radially symmetric and is the load-bearing identity feature.
No repetition system: a single instance, scoring repetitionDensity 0.
One material family in two albedo zones (kernel vs rim), materialLayerCount scores 1.
Local detail density scores 1: the groove/lobe fold is the one authored macro-level displacement, no additional micro details at this budget.
Occlusion risk scores 1: the true underside is hidden but assumed flat/unremarkable by construction.
Action readiness scores 0: static showcase prop.
Aggregate 6/24 stays in the simple tier despite the silhouette bump.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Simple tier by part count, but the bilateral fold needs explicit per-sector displacement authoring (not a coordinate-threshold shortcut) since it is the identity-defining feature.

detailInventory.note: Enumerated by hand from the three supplied reference views -- CRIB.md skip rule for a single simple body.

details.observation: Two rounded lobes separated by a deep central groove running the full long-axis length, giving a wrinkled-brain-like fold.
details.inference: This is the load-bearing identity cue -- a smooth dome without this fold reads as a generic brown blob, not a walnut.

details.observation: Oval footprint, long axis roughly 1.36x the short axis, with the groove running along the long axis.
A thin darker flat band runs around the base perimeter, distinct from the lighter lobed top.
details.inference: The flat underside/rim of the kernel half where it would rest on a surface.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: The true underside (facing away from the camera at every reviewed azimuth) is assumed flat and unremarkable, per the rim band's flat cross-section.
The runtime normalizes the longest axis to 1.6, so absolute dimensions are arbitrary and only the authored ratios carry meaning.
The groove's exact depth/width ratio is not identity-critical at pixel precision; its presence and camera-facing orientation are what the review scores.

surfaceDetail.normalPattern: faceted planar shading from split vertices
surfaceDetail.displacementPattern: cos(2*theta) sector-height modulation on FACE rings for the two-lobe/groove fold -- shape otherwise carried by the revolved elliptical profile

componentTree.name: Walnut kernel dome (two-lobe + groove)
componentTree.topologyRationale: Continuous domed mass revolved from an elliptical profile, with a per-sector height modulation (not a separate solid) carrying the two-lobe/groove fold -- decision tree step 6. Not a sphere/box primitive because the reference's identity-defining feature is the bilateral fold, which only a sector-varying displacement on a revolved base carries.

deformationStack.notes: cos(2*theta)*GROOVE_AMP*ringWeight added to Y on rings [3, 4, 5, 6] (weights [0.35, 0.65, 0.9, 1.0]), theta = sector angle before the whole-body yaw. Lobes at theta=0/180deg (world +-X), groove at theta=90/270deg (world +-Z, the long axis) -- the two groove meridians together trace the line x=0 across the whole long axis, i.e. one continuous groove.
Uniform per-vertex noise, amplitude 0.016 (0.036 of short-axis radius), applied indexed so the rim/dome shared boundary never tears (R1).

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Hard consumer budget for the 'single' ingredient group: 200-500 tri and <=48KB target, hard ceiling <=2500 tri/<=100KB. Target reached by construction (18 segments x 7 profile transitions = 216 tri before the groove modulation, which adds zero triangles), not by decimation.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Warm directional key 0xffe2b0 at (-2, 6, 2), intensity 1.4, upper-left.
lightingFromPhoto.exposure: no tone mapping -- authored albedo lands on screen almost unchanged.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Ambient 0xfff0dc at 0.75 -- the groove/underside darkening relies on the shell's own curvature turning away from the key light.
Cool directional fill 0xdce8ff at (2.5, 3, -2), intensity 0.2, opposite the key.

proceduralStrategy: Revolve the shell from one elliptical profile (pole, base edge, rim-wall-top, four dome rings, crown pole).
Add cos(2*theta) height modulation on the dome rings before jitter, weighted per ring, to carve the two-lobe/groove fold.
Bake a whole-body yaw rotation so the groove crosses the review camera diagonally instead of edge-on.
Jitter vertices while the shell is still indexed, so the rim/kernel split never tears.
Bake faceting by splitting vertices and recomputing normals; never request flatShading.
Slice the rim (bottom fan + first wall band) into its own triangle range after facet() for the rim material.
Project dome UVs per bucket, then merge by material into exactly two meshes.
Translate the whole shell's own bounding box floor to world Y=0.
animationAnchors: root pivot supports whole-body rotation for the showcase turntable
destructionAnchors: single fractureGroup; no plausible sub-fracture for a walnut half

risks.description: assets/prompts/ingredients/walnut.json names #9A6E42 for 'inside the folds and grooves', but this spec applies it to the flat rim/underside band instead.
risks.mitigation: The groove is a geometric concavity that the runtime key light already darkens via N.L falloff (same as the dropped #E0C79A ridge highlight); painting the groove a second dark tone would double-darken it (olive shaded-underside precedent). The rim band is the one OTHER geometrically-distinct flat region in the reference images and reads as a consistent darker edge in all 3 views, so the hex is relocated there rather than dropped outright.

risks.description: assets/prompts/ingredients/walnut.json names #E0C79A for 'raised ridges', which this spec does not wire to a material bucket.
risks.mitigation: Convex lobe crests already catch the runtime key light more brightly via N.L falloff -- painting a highlight color would be redundant with the lighting model.

risks.description: Any vertex-color-based region paint is silently discarded by the runtime's MeshLambertMaterial swap.
risks.mitigation: The kernel/rim split is carried by two separate materials on two separate triangle ranges from one shared indexed shell. No vertexPaint block is authored anywhere.

risks.description: A flatShading flag is not inherited by the runtime material swap.
risks.mitigation: Faceting is baked into geometry by splitting vertices (lib.facet) before export.

risks.description: Rim and kernel triangles come from the same shell; jittering after the triangle-range slice would let the shared boundary move independently.
risks.mitigation: Jitter runs once, on the whole indexed shell, before facet()/slice.

risks.description: If the crown pole height exceeds the modulated lobe-ring peak, the front silhouette reads as a single center spike instead of a valley between two lobes.
risks.mitigation: Crown pole set to heightFraction 0.84 (Y=0.521), verified below the ring6 lobe peak (0.80*0.62+0.09=0.586) by construction. Caught in pre-render review, not left to the cmp loop.
